problem: End-to-end RL object-goal agents suffer from implicit memory decay over long horizons and revisit explored areas, while prior map-based methods ignore visibility constraints and do not balance exploring vs. checking promising areas, giving suboptimal search trajectories.
motivation: Efficient object search in large, unexplored environments with small open-vocabulary objects (OVMM) needs both quick exploration and close inspection of likely locations. Humans peek into rooms and closely check promising spots, so the authors want an explicit, visibility-aware utility that encodes this. Exact computation is rendering-like and too slow, so it needs a learned approximation.
key_idea: Score candidate map locations with a Probable Object Location (POLo) score, which sums object probabilities over visible voxels and mixes exploration and exploitation terms, and approximate this score with a U-Net (POLoNet) for real-time next-goal selection.
insight: Balancing exploration and exploitation matters: pure max-coverage and pure max-object-probability agents both do worse than POLo (SR 12.95 and 10.94 vs 20.31). 3D maps beat 2D projection (POLo-2D SR 13.20 vs 17.71-20.31 for the 3D variants), and higher beta (more exploitation) raises SR and CP/D (SR 16.23, 17.71, 20.31 for beta=1, 3, 5). POLoNet reaches about the same SR as the exact POLo-R (17.71 at beta=3 vs POLo-R at beta=5), at a 76x speedup, and skip connections and data augmentation each reduce MAE.
method: 3D object probability map: 5cm voxels; per-step detection likelihood from Detic scores of goal and receptacle (distance-weighted); fused into the global map with a per-voxel Bayesian update.

POLo score: for a candidate 2D configuration, sums f(p,zeta)=p/d over visible unmapped voxels below threshold delta (exploration) plus beta times the sum over voxels at or above delta (exploitation), multiplied by exp(-lambda*path cost); assumes 360-degree view.
Goal selection: the agent navigates to the map location with the highest POLo score; visibility is computed by voxel rendering with PyTorch3D.

POLoNet: a U-Net-like network with skip connections and 2D convolutions (height treated as channels, 15x192x192 input). It outputs a 2-channel dense POLo map, one channel per score term, and is trained on 19,726 map pairs with labels rendered at 150 random locations, using rotation/translation augmentation.

Variants and metrics: POLo-2D (2D projected maps), POLo-R (exact POLo at 150 sampled locations), and new E/D (explored area per distance) and CP/D (closely checked promising area per distance) metrics.

setting.backbone: POLoNet (U-Net-like CNN, trained) + Detic open-vocabulary detector + heuristic/modular navigation
setting.training_data: 19,726 (occupancy map, probability map, POLo label) pairs from 38 OVMM training scenes; labels computed by the exact POLo formula
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + GPS/compass; builds a 3D occupancy map and an object probability map
setting.action_space: discrete MOVE FORWARD / TURN LEFT / TURN RIGHT / STOP, with high-level map-location goals
setting.privileged: none (a ground-truth-perception ablation is reported separately)

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 episodes from 12 novel scenes of the test dataset; 1250-step budget
numbers.extra: POLoNet trained on 38 training scenes; only the navigation phase of OVMM is evaluated
numbers.evidence: Table II (Evaluation Metrics on the Habitat Simulator), POLoNet (beta=5) row

numbers.backbone: exact POLo via PyTorch3D at 150 sampled locations + Detic
numbers.extra: non-learned POLo computation, restricted to 150 sampled locations

numbers_note: Only the OVMM navigation-phase benchmark is reported (not a canonical benchmark name). Text also states SR rises to 56.7% with ground-truth perception (not tabulated).
results: POLoNet (beta=5) reaches 20.31% SR and 0.083 SPL, beating RL (12.50 / 0.060), FBE (10.99 / 0.049), Max Coverage (12.95 / 0.051) and Max Object Prob. (10.94 / 0.054). POLoNet computes scores in 0.26s vs 20s for the exact computation (76x faster) with test MAE 0.0117.
limitations: Absolute success rates are low (~20%), mainly due to perception failures on small objects (SR 56.7% with ground-truth perception) and low-level controller collisions in narrow corridors and doors.
Evaluated only in simulation on 200 episodes from 12 scenes, with no real-robot tests; POLoNet is trained on a small dataset labeled at sparse locations (150 per map).
Assumes a 360-degree field of view and voxel independence, and ignores view angle; beta must be tuned.
builds_on: Next-best-view exploration (Bircher et al. receding horizon)
